name: Open-interest flush + oversold rebound — buy the forced-deleverage capitulation (spot long)
rationale: MECHANISM (why the derivative leads price): a sharp DROP in open_interest is the fingerprint of forced deleveraging — margin calls and liquidations closing leveraged positions en masse. That flush IS the capitulation: once the over-levered longs are gone, the marginal seller is exhausted and price snaps back. OI (a perp-derived read) turns at the liquidation event slightly before spot price finishes bottoming, so open_interest cross_down through a fitted (normalized) floor is an early bottom tag. We require a price confirmation — RSI oversold — so we buy a genuine washout, not a slow orderly bleed, and take it on SPOT (no perp-short needed). Exit on RSI reverting up (bounce played out) or stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: the edge must be the OI FLUSH, not generic oversold — if dropping the open_interest arm and keeping only RSI-oversold matches the deflated Sharpe, OI adds nothing. DISCONFIRMER 2: OI falls mechanically as price falls; if replacing the RSI-oversold arm with an RSI-strong arm flips the sign, OI is just a price proxy, not a deleverage signal. Net of ~20bps round-trip the bounce must still pay.
catalyst: open_interest crashes DOWN through a fitted floor (leverage flushed / longs liquidated) while RSI is oversold — a washed-out bottom.
